symptom: Synthetic Python jsonschema Draft 2020-12 accepts a trailing LF after Outcome Ledger settledAt and sourceEvidenceDigests values because regex dollar can match before a final newline; the Node runtime rejects both noncanonical values. This is a schema-only cross-engine lexical mismatch, not observed private data corruption or a production incident.
lesson: A JSON Schema regex dollar anchor does not guarantee exact terminal matching in Python: a final LF can be admitted despite runtime rejection. Schema-only evidence consumers must not treat lexical acceptance as authenticated settlement or provenance.
guardrail: Reuse the K1 and Shadow Evidence portable exact-end assertion (?![\s\S]) for Outcome Ledger settledAt and sourceEvidenceDigests; retain positive canonical controls plus LF, CRLF and Unicode terminator negative regressions. Keep runtime date and digest validation authoritative, with productionConnection=false.
